key: folk:snake:The Trench Leviathan|serpent|tsunami|blue|A rocky Oregon coastline, 3:33 AM|

narrator.persona: a thirty-year-old lighthouse keeper telling it a year later

sentences.text: If a heavy tremor follows you at night on the coast, don't look back.
sentences.speaker: narrator

sentences.text: I was checking the diesel logs when the tide simply vanished, leaving bare mud and gasping fish where deep water used to be.
sentences.speaker: narrator

sentences.text: My deputy radioed from the cliff road before the signal died completely.
sentences.speaker: narrator

sentences.text: Run inland now, the harbor is completely gone!
sentences.speaker: person

sentences.text: A towering mountain of black brine rose out of the dark trench, carrying weed and bone in its crest.
sentences.speaker: narrator

sentences.text: Four emerald eyes blinked open within the churning wall, staring right through the reinforced glass of the tower.
sentences.speaker: narrator

sentences.text: The massive creature crested the ridge, blotting out the stars as it stared down at the trembling earth.
sentences.speaker: narrator

sentences.text: Would you still hear the sound of the retreating sea in your sleep every single night?
sentences.speaker: narrator
